sources.title: New opportunities to earn and changes to the YouTube Partner Program
sources.used_for: Aug 10 2026 official: 55% revenue share for long-form vs 45% Shorts; from Feb 1 2027 10M qualified Shorts views/90d needed for Shorts ad share; new creators need 8,000 qualified watch hours or 20M qualified Shorts views; existing YPP unaffected.

sources.title: What are qualified watch hours and Shorts views for YPP?
sources.used_for: Qualified watch hours come from public long-form / podcasts / archived livestreams; Shorts watch hours do NOT count; engaged view means viewer stayed past initial seconds and excludes loops.

sources.title: Measure key moments for audience retention
sources.used_for: Intro = % still watching after 30s; Spikes = moments rewatched or shared; Dips = skipped/abandoned; flat = watched start to finish; typical retention compares 10 similar-length videos; data takes 1-2 days; video must be >=60s and >=100 views; owner-only video-level Analytics.

sources.title: YouTube performance FAQ & Troubleshooting
sources.used_for: Recommendation system 'finds videos for your audience', ranked by performance + relevance + satisfaction; search results are NOT a most-viewed list; accurate non-clickbait titles/thumbnails; avoid ALL CAPS; tags 'not important'; upload cadence and publish time not correlated with long-term performance; monetization status doesn't affect discovery.

sources.title: YouTube channel monetization policies (Reused / Inauthentic content)
sources.used_for: Official: 'There is no change to our reused content policy which reviews content like commentary, clips, compilations, and reaction videos.' Allowed: clips for critical review, rewritten VO, replays with technique explanation, reactions with commentary, edited footage with storyline + commentary. NOT allowed: clips strung together with little/no narrative, short compilations from other platforms, non-verbal reactions, content with minimal changes, templated/mass-produced output. Reviewers check channel theme, most-viewed videos, newest videos, biggest watch-time proportion, metadata, About.

sources.title: Fair use on YouTube
sources.used_for: Four factors: purpose/character (transformative, nonprofit education favored), nature (factual favored), amount/substantiality ('heart' of work can matter even if short), market effect. Credit alone, disclaimers, 'non-profit' label do NOT create fair use. Only courts decide; Content ID cannot decide fair use; local law differs outside US.

sources.title: Learn about copyright claims / Content ID
sources.used_for: Content ID claims can block, monetize or track; geography-specific; multiple claimants possible for different segments; claims don't usually impact channel; Checks results aren't final.

sources.title: Dispute a copyright claim
sources.used_for: Valid dispute reasons: all necessary rights, copyright exception such as fair use, misidentification. NOT valid: giving credit, owning a copy, choosing not to monetize. Claimant has 30 days; YouTube cannot decide ownership or fair use; seek legal advice.

sources.title: License types on YouTube (Standard / CC BY)
sources.used_for: CC BY requires title, author, source URL and licence info; original content, CC BY content or public domain can be marked CC BY; a Content ID claim prevents CC BY marking; find CC content via advanced search filter.

sources.title: Upload YouTube videos - Computer
sources.used_for: Upload = file imported; Publish = anyone can watch; Private/Unlisted/Public; Category + Education type; title 100 chars / description 5,000; Checks incl. copyright + Likeness detection; 'Copyright check results aren't final'; monetization toggle for YPP; AI-use disclosure.

sources.title: Find playlists & videos using hashtags
sources.used_for: Up to 3 hashtags shown above title; >60 hashtags all ignored; misleading/unrelated hashtags bannable; ordinary descriptive tags or repetitive sentences in description prohibited.

sources.title: Spam Policy / malicious clickbait
sources.used_for: Genuine like/comment/subscribe asks allowed; bots, coercion, rewards, repetitive/deceptive content, maliciously misleading titles/thumbnails and clickbait without payoff banned.

sources.title: Disclosing use of GenAI content
sources.used_for: Disclose realistic AI-altered content via Attributes > AI use (Yes/No); cloning one's own voice for VO/dubs and caption creation are examples NOT needing disclosure; 'Disclosing AI content alone won't limit a video's audience or impact its eligibility to earn money'; non-disclosure can bring penalties.

sources.title: YouTube Shorts monetization policies
sources.used_for: Non-original Shorts (unedited clips from others, reuploads, compilations with no original content) are ineligible views; from Feb 1 2027 10M qualified Shorts views/90d threshold; only monetizing partners who accepted Shorts Monetization Module earn Shorts ad revenue.

sources.title: Choose how you want to monetize
sources.used_for: Turn on ads = 'you confirm that you have all the necessary rights to the visual and audio elements'; turning ads on doesn't mean ads automatically appear (automated/human review); Shorts Feed ads require accepting Shorts Monetization Module in Earn.

sources.title: Turn off ads for individual videos
sources.used_for: Studio > Content > Monetization > Off > Save; can turn off monetization for already-uploaded videos.

sources.title: Stop guessing, start growing: Master these 4 metrics
sources.used_for: CTR = thumbnail/title billboard; high CTR + low retention = thumbnail promised something the video didn't deliver; inspect spikes and slow intros; Test & Compare can be used even on older videos; look for patterns in 'Videos Growing Your Audience' and make 2-3 more like them.
